claim: An absorb whose dossier carries a `population` or an `institutions` value the port cannot read has no safe outcome on a bound map. Round 3 turned both from a refusal (`E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE` before R3-20) into the creation fallback: V08 §2.4's `population` row (l.634: 'empty, or no such integer → the default request of the tier word's rung …, else the one-click default's 5 000'), its `institutions[]` row (l.646: 'a value that is no list (read as absent, noted)'), J-V8.134 (l.3527) and §3.5 step 3 (l.1600-1605). Only the `id` row (l.631) states an absorb-time fallback ('at an absorb the bound document's settlement key'). `population`, `institutions[]`, `name` and `tier` state only the creation value. V08 §3.5's diff (l.1665-1675) then compares the carried facts with the new digest. The settlement row's `population` → `population` makes an epoch whose target is the tier word's default. Every carried institution key now absent makes `remove` with fate `vanished`, closing every dossier-bound use, locked buildings' included (§7.7 item 14). `name` → `rename`. A port epoch is no undo, redo or revert target (V08 §2.7, l.1291), and the next readable dossier raises the population back and reopens each institution (F6). So one unreadable value rewrites the map twice. The same subsection gives the opposite outcome for an unreadable record: when a quarantined record's key cannot be formed, 'every carried institution key absent from the new digest is held — no `remove` — … until a readable dossier arrives' (l.1666-1668). Item 125 (b) asks for 'the generator's own choice, exactly as on a map made without a dossier', and on a bound map made without a dossier nothing changes the population or the institutions. §3.17's rows (l.2643, l.2657), T-V8-61 and §7.7 item 10 state the fallback without the absorb case.
required_change: 1. V08 §3.5's diff, after the quarantine sentence, adds: 'At an absorb, a value of a required key that took its field-table fallback — `population`, `name` or `tier` empty or unreadable, an `institutions` that is no list (V08 §2.4) — makes no change: the carried fact stands. The settlement row compares nothing for that field, and every carried institution key is held, no `remove`, as a quarantined record's are. One `field_fallback` note names the field with "the map kept its record's last value", until a readable value arrives. The field table's fallback values serve a creation.' 2. V08 §2.4's `population`, `name`, `tier` and `institutions[]` rows each add to their fallback cell '— at an absorb, the carried value (V08 §3.5)'. 3. J-V8.134 adds 'at an absorb the carried value stands for every such field, as the `id` row's bound key does'. 4. §3.17's 'the digest and the diff' row and 'the one input and its fallbacks' row add the case 'an absorb whose `population`, `name`, `tier` or `institutions` is empty or unreadable', with the outcome 'the carried value kept, no change, noted `field_fallback`'. 5. T-V8-61 (a) adds: 'on `city-1` after its creation, an absorb whose `population` is emptied and whose `institutions` is an object keeps the carried population and every institution — no epoch, no `remove`, no `rename`, the model digest unchanged — each noted `field_fallback`, and the next readable dossier absorbs as usual'.

claim: V08 §2.4's `recognise` (rewritten this round) accepts only with 'every requiredKeys key present', and `select` runs at `digest`'s step 1 (V08 §3.5), before steps 2–3. A dossier missing one required key is therefore accepted by no adapter, and `select` refuses it `E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED` — B5 'no registered adapter accepts the dossier' — so step 3's 'a key's own absence → `E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE` listing up to 20 violations (B3)' is never reached. T-V8-31 bars 'a dossier missing one required key is refused `E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE`'. B3, §3.16 (9) (b) ('A required key's own absence stays a shape the line never writes (B3)'), the field table's lead, J-V8.134 and V08 §3.17's messages row ('a `dossier.offer` without `dossier` is `E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE` (B3)') say B3. Base §14 port item 2 says 'A shape no adapter recognises is refused `E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE` (a hand-made teaching file among them), a line no adapter serves `E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED`'. One case has two outcomes, with different held messages ('could not be read' against 'version is not supported'), and T-V8-31 cannot pass as the steps are written. repair-r3-V08 note 9 hands this to this round. It predates the round but lies in the subsections the round rewrote (§2.4's `recognise` and *Selection*, §3.5 steps 1 and 3).
required_change: V08 §2.4: where no registered adapter accepts, `select` refuses `E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE` (B3) when the dossier lacks a `requiredKeys` key of every registered adapter — no dossier of any registered line (a required key absent; §14's hand-made teaching file; an offer without a dossier) — and otherwise `E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED` naming the candidates (B5). Texts: `select`'s refused branch reads `{ status: 'refused'; code: 'E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE' | 'E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED'; candidates: string[] }`. *Selection*'s '`E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED` naming the candidates only when none accepts' → 'when none accepts, `E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE` listing up to 20 violations (B3) where the dossier lacks a required key of every registered adapter, else `E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED` naming the candidates (B5)'. §3.5 step 1's 'a refusal ends the call (`E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED`)' → 'a refusal ends the call (`E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE` or `E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED`, V08 §2.4)'. Step 3's first sentence → 'Every `requiredKeys` key present — a key's absence is refused at step 1, `E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE` (B3).' B3's detection cell 'V08 §3.5 steps 2–3' → '`select` (V08 §2.4: a required key absent) and V08 §3.5 step 2 (a limit)'. B5's cause 'no registered adapter accepts the dossier' → 'no registered adapter accepts a dossier holding every required key of one'. T-V8-31 stands. T-V8-14's forcing of B3 adds a dossier missing one required key, and of B5 one whose readable `schemaVersion` no registered adapter serves.

claim: Round 3 made a `population` 'no integer in [0, 10⁷]' an unreadable value that takes the field-table fallback. The texts are the field table's `population` row ('read as an integer in [0, 10⁷] …: empty, or no such integer → the default request of the tier word's rung …'), §3.5 step 3, and §3.17's digest row ('a population above 10⁷, or one no integer, takes its field-table fallback'). Base §1.1 says 'a dossier above it [the 120 000 cap] is refused by the port the same way, `E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE` naming the population cap, at creation and at every absorb'; §14 port item 3 and V08's own B7 say the same. So a dossier of 20 000 000 people makes a map at the tier word's default under V08, and is refused under the base and B7. One of 9 999 999 is refused by both: the outcome is not monotonic in the population. Item 125 (b)'s fallback serves a missing or empty value, and a readable whole number above the cap is neither. Before this round the case was a refusal (`E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE`). The wording is this seat's round-2 required change (G125-V08 (2)), adopted by R3-20 (2); the cap rule was missed.
